mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median 20-day return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month triggers a demand-pull recession signal, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average 60-day return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during a technology-led market rally.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding rise in unemployment, signals supply-side disruption rather than demand weakness, which historically precedes short-term equity market volatility and negative returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m < -1% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE m/m <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 registers positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of geopolitical conflict.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3% month-over-month signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes higher wage inflation and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% for three consecutive months, coupled with flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), indicates a precautionary savings regime that suppresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS m/m > 5% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 m/m <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which typically supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS m/m < -0.5% AND UNRATE m/m > 0.3% (indicating recession)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 6% for six consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining industrial production (INDPRO), signals a high-inflation stagnation regime that erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 6% for 6 consecutive months AND INDPRO m/m <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 registers positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.
